purpose: Determine what a succession or ownership event changes, what remains separately registered, and what evidence is required before stating the resulting title position.
source_basis: Registration of Title Act 1964, as amended
Land Registration Rules 2012 to 2013 and applicable later amendments

event_consequences.immediate_effect: Succession and estate-administration consequences arise; the final beneficiary's registered title is not established merely by the death.
event_consequences.registration_question: Identify the personal representative and applicable testate/intestate route, then verify the registration outcome.

event_consequences.immediate_effect: Creates the relevant succession instrument for the registration process.
event_consequences.registration_question: Check whether and when the register was actually changed.

event_consequences.immediate_effect: Potential survivorship route; the deceased joint tenant's name may be withdrawn following prescribed proof.
event_consequences.registration_question: Verify the folio's ownership structure and the death evidence before treating the survivor as the sole registered owner.

event_consequences.immediate_effect: The deceased's distinct share enters the succession analysis rather than being treated as automatic joint-tenancy survivorship.
event_consequences.registration_question: Identify the share and succession route, then verify registration.

event_consequences.immediate_effect: The right to be registered may have devolved even though the folio has not yet been updated.
event_consequences.registration_question: Determine whether section 90 powers are engaged and whether the statutory conditions are satisfied.

event_consequences.immediate_effect: A disposal by the estate is distinct from transmission to a beneficiary.
event_consequences.registration_question: Follow the disposal and purchaser-registration route; do not describe the beneficiary as owner merely because they were named in a will.

interaction_rules.rule: Inheritance or transfer does not by itself prove that a registered charge has been discharged. Inspect the burden and separate discharge/transfer evidence.
Always determine whether the registered ownership was joint or in common before applying a death route.
A transfer or succession event does not by itself establish the creation, alteration or extinction of an easement; inspect the relevant burden/appurtenance and underlying instrument where necessary.
A title transfer does not itself resolve a disputed boundary. The statutory register/map rules must be considered separately.
Current register data must not be used as a substitute for reconstructing an earlier title state where the question concerns a historical event.

answer_matrix.question: Am I now the registered owner?
Did the house pass to me when the owner died?
Can the beneficiary sell before registration?
Did the mortgage disappear after inheritance?

guardrails: Never convert a succession entitlement into a current registered-proprietor statement without current authoritative registration evidence.
Never treat the absence of a beneficiary's name from a current folio as proof that the beneficiary has no succession entitlement.
Never treat a will, probate, assent or transfer as a substitute for the relevant register evidence when the question is current registered title.
Never infer discharge of a mortgage or other burden from inheritance or sale alone.
Never apply survivorship without verifying the ownership form.
Never resolve historical title from a current snapshot alone.
